finding.claim: With nestTables: true, a result set whose table name is __proto__ makes parseRowNested write row['__proto__'][column] = value, which resolves to Object.prototype and pollutes it process-wide. Preconditions: nestTables opt-in, and a server-supplied or DB-created table named __proto__.
finding.source: Column-definition metadata table name (lib/cmd/column-definition.js:143-144, _readIdentifier(1)), server-controlled or created by any DB user with CREATE privilege (second-order).

trace.note: table() returns the server-sent table identifier
nestTables===true selects parseRowNested and builds tableHeader[i] = [table, name]
table name stored without filtering __proto__, constructor or prototype
row['__proto__'] is Object.prototype (truthy), so the {} initializer is skipped
Object.prototype[name] = parsed value, global pollution

finding.guards_checked: checkNestTablesDuplicates (parser.js:328-339) runs only under checkDuplicate and does not filter keys. No key allowlist or Object.create(null) on row. Same unfiltered row[key]= pattern in parseRowStdText (parser.js:553-557) and parseRowStdBinary (parser.js:562-566), which affects per-row prototype for object values. Not reachable with nestTables off except per-row.

finding.claim: Server-directed redirect is enabled by default (permitRedirect defaults to true). A server or proxy can send redirect_url and move the client to an arbitrary host, which receives the user's credentials (native-password scramble) and then all later SQL and bound parameters.
finding.source: redirect_url in OK packets (lib/cmd/parser.js:169-171, 195-199) and post-auth session state (lib/cmd/handshake/authentication.js:100-103).
finding.sink: Reconnect with credentials to an attacker-chosen host (lib/connection.js:1633), then socket/info swap into the original connection (lib/connection.js:1641-1647).

trace.note: permitRedirect defaults to true
redirect_url from OK packet session state
new URL(value) on server string
host taken from URL with no allowlist
Object.assign copies original user and password into the new connection options
original connection adopts the attacker host socket, info and opts

finding.guards_checked: Protocol check (connection.js:1606) and same-host skip (connection.js:1621) only. No host allowlist, no user confirmation. Cleartext plugin guard (authentication.js:203) still blocks mysql_clear_password over plaintext TCP. Requires a malicious server or proxy, or plaintext MITM.

finding.claim: pool.escape falls back to backslash escaping when the pool has no idle connection, even if active connections exist, because _searchInfo iterates array indices instead of connection IDs. Under a server with NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES, a value like x\' OR 1=1 -- breaks out of the string literal (SQL injection).
finding.source: Application value passed to pool.escape / pool-promise.escape / pool-callback.escape, e.g. user-supplied input under load.
finding.sink: Single-quoted literal produced by escapeString (lib/misc/utils.js:247-258) when info is null, reached via lib/pool.js:504.

trace.note: activeConnections is an object keyed by threadId
for...in over Object.keys(...) yields indices '0','1'... which do not match thread IDs, so conn stays undefined
conn falsy, so info stays null
Utils.escape receives null info
info null means noBackslashEscapes false, backslash escaping chosen

finding.guards_checked: escapeString checks info != null for NO_BACKSLASH mode, but null info is treated as backslash mode. Per-connection writer (packet-output-stream.js:378-390) reads the real status and is correct, so the bug is limited to pool.escape / pool wrappers. Requires server NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES and a pool with no idle connection at the time of the call.

finding.claim: With permitSetMultiParamEntries enabled, object keys are written into backtick identifiers without escaping. A key containing a backtick injects SQL. The same unescaped write is in the text encoder.
finding.source: Object keys of a value passed as a ? parameter, e.g. req.body used in UPDATE t SET ?, when the application does not control key names.
finding.sink: Identifier written as '`' + key + '`=' in escapeParameters (lib/misc/utils.js:213) and '`' + key + '`' in TextEncoder.writeParam (lib/cmd/encoder/text-encoder.js:135).

trace.note: permitSetMultiParamEntries opt-in flag
for...in over attacker-influenced object keys
key concatenated into a backtick identifier without doubling backticks
same unescaped key write on the query path

finding.guards_checked: Only the opt-in option gate. Compare escapeId (lib/misc/utils.js:106) which doubles backticks and rejects NUL; this path does not use it. Requires the option enabled and attacker-controlled object keys.
